decision:
NARROWED. I support the refute and data verifiers (NARROWED) over the rederive verifier (OPEN). The audit's grade is superseded on its own stated terms.

Why the audit's OPEN no longer holds:
- The audit graded OPEN because Juarez-Aubry 2011.05947 and 2412.08402 were NAMED-NOT-READ and the discover_papers sweep had not run.
- Its what_would_change_the_grade names NARROWED as the expected ceiling once those papers are read and a sweep finds nothing contrary.
- The rederive verifier's OPEN rests on the same two unread papers, and its own text says NARROWED needs them read and a sweep done.
- Both conditions are now met. I READ both papers at source this pass (alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries, full page text). The sweep has now run three times: one call by the refute verifier and two by me.

The evidence, all READ or computed:

(1) 2412.08402v2 (Juarez-Aubry, dated 1 Dec 2025), READ pp.1-6.
- Theorem 1: at xi = 1/2, for a special class of Hadamard two-point functions ('perhaps up to positivity'), there is a unique analytic Cauchy evolution with no symmetry assumed. The two-point function is reconstructed only in a causal normal neighbourhood N of C.
- Sec. VI, verbatim: 'local semiclassical gravity solutions exist for every (analytic) vacuum solution of higher-derivative gravity (and of general relativity!), modulo state positivity'.
- Also verbatim: positivity 'remains an important open question'.
- The paper never names Schwarzschild. Applying sec. VI to Schwarzschild is the verifiers' step and mine.
- That step is checked by computation. Schwarzschild is Ricci-flat with K = 48M^2/r^6, so it is non-flat (A2). With all alpha = 0, eq. (III.3) gives <T> = 0 = G, so (IV.1a) holds. (IV.1b) is then a linear Klein-Gordon equation for w0 with non-zero source -2 v1 = -(m^4/4 + 2M^2/(15 r^6)) (A4).
- So in a relaxed sector (xi = 1/2, positivity open, local on N, analytic), a READ general existence theorem yields non-flat static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat members. In that sector the tree's unqualified 'which nobody has' is false. That is a hypothesis the tree drops, i.e. NARROWED.
- It is not a refutation: this is not a theorem for positive Hadamard states, nor at HPS's xi = 1/6.

(2) 2011.05947v2, READ.
- Prop. 9 (p.18) is a no-go. A static, Ricci-flat, globally hyperbolic spacetime other than Minkowski admits no states for the conformally coupled field (m = 0, xi = 1/6) that solve the equations, for any alpha and beta. The paper names Schwarzschild.
- The mechanism is computed: eq. (6.14) needs K/720 to be constant, and it is not (A3).
- This is a partial no-go in HPS's coupling, for Ricci-flat geometries only.

(3) Other sources agree that no general theorem exists in the positive-state exact class:
- Sanders 2007.14311v2 p.2;
- 2604.01047v1 p.13, read live: 'a general theory for the well-posedness ... is missing';
- 2412.08402 p.1: rigorous results 'only in highly symmetric spacetimes'.

(4) My sweep returned only numerical work or work with an approximate or modified source.
- 2212.09375v2, READ: order-reduced AHS source. p.12 says HPS's solution is the only known non-perturbative AHS-sourced solution, and it is not asymptotically flat.
- 2506.17149v1, READ: an objective-collapse framework, with no existence theorem.
- The rest are abstract-only.

(5) The wording discrepancies were re-computed.
- 'Only' is overstated. The no-go route decides O5 under either encoding of 'existence theorem' (A5), so the overstatement is robust.
- The audit's C3c holds only under the 'some non-trivial member' encoding.

Why not each other grade:
- Not STANDS: the tree drops the source-term, positivity and coupling hypotheses that 2412.08402 makes load-bearing, and it keeps 'only'.
- Not WRONG: no READ paper proves a non-flat static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat solution for a positive Hadamard state with exact renormalised <T>. A relaxed-sector theorem is not a counterexample in the tree's own context, which is HPS's xi = 1/6 system.
- Not OPEN: every grade condition the audit named is now READ or run. The residue is a universal negative, carried as the tree's own named hypothesis 'NOT-FOUND, not NO' (throatmass.py:40-58) on a recorded search. It is not presumed.
- Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no measured datum enters. The HPS fit does not move the conclusion (F(1e3) = 123.457, F(1e6) = 2277.409, F -> infinity).
scope:
COVERS throatmass.py:98-99 ('Closed only by a general existence theorem for the static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat class, which nobody has') and its restatement at throatmass.py:174-176.

Under these named hypotheses, the claim holds as NOT-FOUND:
- (H-a) The source is the exact renormalised <T> of a POSITIVE Hadamard state, not a two-point function 'modulo positivity'.
- (H-b) The coupling is outside the xi = 1/2 stealth sector, for example HPS's xi = 1/6, m = 0. There, 2011.05947 Prop. 9 is a READ no-go for every Ricci-flat non-Minkowski static member.
- (H-c) Existence means non-trivial (non-flat) existence, or existence for prescribed data, because Minkowski is a member.
- (H-d) The solution is global, not confined to a neighbourhood N of a Cauchy surface.
- (H-e) 'Only' is dropped.

The NOT-FOUND is a floor. It rests on READ sources up to April 2026 and three discover_papers calls. It is not proof that no such theorem exists.

DOES NOT COVER:
- (i) Existence theory for HPS's actual system, which uses the AHS approximate <T>. No READ source settles it either way.
- (ii) Whether the stealth two-point functions are positive.
- (iii) The journal versions (PLB 875 (2026) 140349; AHP 23 (2022) 1451), which were not compared with the arXiv versions.
- (iv) O5 itself.
- (v) The six sweep hits known only from abstracts.
corrections_to_record: The audit's data row ('Nothing READ shows that [the stealth class of 2412.08402 contains a non-flat static spherically symmetric asymptotically flat member]') is SUPERSEDED. 2412.08402v2 is now READ (Thm 1 pp.4-5; sec. VI p.6). Its claim that local solutions exist 'for every (analytic) vacuum solution of ... general relativity!, modulo state positivity' covers Schwarzschild. Schwarzschild being non-flat and satisfying (IV.1a) with all alpha = 0 is COMPUTED (adjudicator A2/A4; refute check.py). The paper never names Schwarzschild, so the member is an application of the paper's statement, not a quotation. It holds only at xi = 1/2, with positivity open, locally on N, for analytic data.

2011.05947 is not a paper that 'suggests the gap may be closing'. READ: Prop. 9 (p.18) is a no-go for m = 0, xi = 1/6 on every static, Ricci-flat, globally hyperbolic non-Minkowski spacetime, for any alpha and beta, and it names Schwarzschild. Its effect is 'confirms, partially' (Ricci-flat only), not 'extends'. The eq. (6.14) mechanism is computed (A3).

The audit's 'DROPPED QUALIFIER non-trivial' overstates the case against the tree. The tree says 'a GENERAL existence theorem', and one trivial Minkowski member does not contradict that. This sharpens the unstated scope (H2); it is not a discrepancy in the tree's wording.

The audit's C3c ('an existence theorem alone is consistent with both answers') depends on the encoding. It holds for E = 'some non-trivial AF member'. For E = 'every admissible datum, m<0 data included, is realised', E implies O5 (A5, with a vacuity guard). 'Only' is overstated robustly through the no-go route. C3a is true by construction.

Audit C1 tests the HPS eqs (5)-(7) transcription only weakly: a flat profile kills every derivative term, and the control residual comes mostly from the left-hand side (rederive verifier V1-V3). C1's conclusion stands independently, because Sanders p.2 and 2011.05947 sec. 6.1 both name Minkowski as a solution.

Discrepancy recorded, not repaired: HPS gr-qc/9701064v1 eq. (6) has, inside its ln f bracket, the term '-4 f'^2 r'^2/(f^2 r)'. Its dimension is L^-3, while every other term is L^-4. READ this pass, and A1 shows it is the only inhomogeneous term in eqs (5)-(7). It is likely a misprint of r for r^2. It does not affect C1 or eq. (8), and the audit transcribed it faithfully.

The audit's use of Sanders sec. 7 ('or even in general static spacetimes') as leaving the existence of static solutions open is a misreading. That sentence concerns the ground state's special role for general states.

The audit's 'confirms' from 2604.01047v1 rested on a harvest that lacks page 13. Page 13, now READ live, supports the conclusion: 'a general theory for the well-posedness of the Cauchy problem on arbitrary background and for arbitrary Cauchy data is missing'.

'discover_papers NOT RUN' is superseded: there were three calls, one by the refute verifier and two by the adjudicator. None found an existence theorem for the exact class. 2212.09375v2 and 2506.17149v1 were READ; six other hits are abstract-only.

HPS's abstract ('two asymptotically spatially flat regions') and p.8 ('the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat') are both true: the first is about R(l) -> l, the second about the unbounded f. A write-up should quote p.8, not the abstract.
